commits.message:
Attach operator-2's node to a public stack as a loopback second instance

A second instance now attaches to a preprod-rehearsal or preprod-public
stack. It names its own private node configuration (nodeConfigFile, the
six node secrets, none of them in its .env) and an https:// loopback
endpoint, and runs the stack's release: the release revision, public
origin and node, Postgres and ingress images come from the stack's .env,
which its own may only repeat. Its node runs from the stack's node image,
serves the stack's TLS certificate and mounts the stack's signed release,
TLS files and trust roots read-only; every host port, the node API's
included, is on loopback, it builds no image and never starts ingress.

Loading refuses an operator or merge wallet off the compiled allow-list,
another profile than the stack's, a validation worker pool below 2 or
disabled rate limits, and a node directory, run directory or node
configuration that would lie in (or hold) the stack's release directory.
A run refuses to start its node before the stack has signed its release,
since Docker would otherwise create the missing mount source.

The public node's .env, secret-loading, limit and allow-list checks move
into helpers the primary and the second instance share. Adds the
operator-2 rehearsal example, its drill steps, and the two merge wallets
in the rehearsal funding table.
Say that the late-shift lead beyond its minimum is the commit's window

Allow-list one merge key per operator on the Preprod production profiles

preprod-rehearsal and preprod-public list each operator's wallet and its
merge wallet (2 -> 4 payment key hashes), regenerated with preprod-testing
kept as the selected profile. The generated profile module's size cap in
the declarative table moves from 632 to 636 lines for the four new list
entries.

End the late-shift window where the fault's header still ends in the shift

A late or retried commit started up to a commit allowance before the shift
ended could build a fault header ending past operator-2's shift. The window
now closes at the shift's end less the shortest lead, plus one millisecond,
so both the commit and the header end inside the shift.

Announce a public stack's retained DA at its public DNS name

A preprod-rehearsal or preprod-public stack now names the public DNS name
of its retained DA (public.retainedDaHost), refused by name when missing,
local, private or an IP address. Its committee manifests announce the
retained DA as /dns4 on the retained-transport port, listening on every
interface, so the stack's watcher, whose public-endpoint rule is unchanged
for production, accepts it.

A preprod-testing stack's watcher reaches its retained DA on loopback
through the generated watcher setting da.stackLoopbackPeers, which admits
loopback IPv4 peers only and which a production build's watcher refuses by
name (production_profile_refused).

Document removing an old-format pending ledger-owner deposit record

A pending deposit recorded by an older drill has no transaction hash or
validity end; the drill stops on it. The fault drill inputs now say which
file to remove by hand and what happens next.

Require a late-shift lead that covers the fault header's end

A staged fault's header ends up to a minute after it is built, so a lead
shorter than the commit allowance plus 60,000 ms could put the header past
operator-2's shift. The drill now refuses such a lead up front, naming
STACK_LATE_SHIFT_LEAD_MS and the bound, and the header's end offset is a
named constant shared with staging.

Start the fault-tail window at our node's first landed_block_invalid

A shift of ours that ended before our node knew the fault invalid says
nothing about its refusal to build on it, so the overlap window now opens
at the first held observation. The lead measurements stay measured from
the fault's commit, which the record now names.

Prove operator-2's node stopped before each DA publication as its producer

The drill's DA publications use operator-2's producer key, so the session
now guards them like operator-2's wallet signatures: each publication first
proves the node held stopped, and one without that proof is refused before
any transport opens.

Pin the successor's fault binding and the resumed node's follower tip in tests

The other-fault transfer case now checks the retried attempt stages a
transfer bound to this fault, and the removed-node case covers a follower
behind the tip without a catching-up reason, or with no follower at all.

Fail a refusal drill a DA peer rejects for its delivery

A committee peer rejecting the payload for another deployment, another
payload schema or the size bound says nothing about the fault, so the
drill now fails on those codes instead of counting them as a refusal.
Each peer's code stays in the saved delivery.

Stop our node's hold watch on every failed attached journey run

The watch starts at the fault's commit and was stopped only by staging
failures, the successor port and a completed refusal. A failed public DA
preflight or age-out wait left it polling our node. The attached mode now
closes it from the run's finally.

Bound the runbook's node-start check to the preflight function's body

The check that node-start.ts still runs producer-da-preflight matched from
the preflightProducerTransport declaration to the id anywhere after it, so
the id in a later function passed it. It now reads only the function's body,
up to its closing brace. The validator takes --full-stack-dir to read a
copy of the stack's sources, and a test edits that copy to prove the check
fails.

Bound the rehearsal example's waits to four hours and rerun for the payout

The 8-day timeout let one run hold the controller across the whole 7-day
block maturity. The example keeps the 4-hour bound every other stack uses;
the drill steps say that a run stopped waiting for the payout is rerun with
the same configuration, and its withdrawal step resumes waiting for the
same payout from its saved receipt.

Recreate DA and node containers when their generated manifest changes

Compose recreates a container on up -d only when its service definition
changes, never when a bind-mounted file's bytes do. A later run that
admitted operator-2 rewrote every committee manifest, yet the committee and
retained-DA containers kept running with the old ones; operator-2's node
likewise kept a stale producer manifest after the stack regenerated its own.
Each service that mounts a generated manifest now carries a label with the
manifest's digest, so its Compose configuration hash changes with the file.
The tests read that hash from docker compose config --hash.
